title: Efficient Single-Source SimRank Query by Path Aggregation

problem.claim: Single-source SimRank queries compute similarity between a query node and every node in a graph by traversing paths from the query node.

gap.claim: Path counts grow exponentially with path length, reducing computation efficiency; sampling-based methods require sufficient path samples for accuracy and can be affected by the resulting path scale.

contributions.claim: VecSim aggregates paths from the query node and arrived nodes to compute hitting and first-meeting probabilities while maintaining only several vectors.
VecSim excludes extra-meeting probabilities at each step and estimates them with a length-bounded sampling algorithm.
A threshold-sieved algorithm prunes entries with small contributions to final similarity scores.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on four small and four large graphs show VecSim has lower time and space costs than competitors at comparable accuracy.
The authors report an empirical error at the 10^-4 level in under 0.1 second across all evaluated graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Single-source SimRank requires path traversal from a query node.
Path growth and sampling requirements limit computational efficiency.
VecSim uses path aggregation, bounded sampling for extra-meeting probabilities, and threshold-based pruning.
Experiments report improved time and space costs at comparable accuracy and low empirical error.

unknowns: The evaluated graph identities, sizes, and structural characteristics are unspecified.
The competitor algorithms and experimental protocol are unspecified.
No theoretical accuracy, complexity, or memory guarantees are provided.
